tasks.short: Design, code, test and document GIS models or mapping applications.

steps.what: Clarify mapping requirements and validation examples
Design the spatial model, interfaces and test specification
Implement the model and mapping interface in a development branch

loop.input: Explicit spatial design, repository conventions, allowed APIs and test fixtures
loop.output: Branch-only implementation candidate with changes explained
loop.check: Technician checks spatial operations, coordinate conversions and access behaviour in s3/s5; independent expected geometries and interaction tests run in s4
loop.stop: One patch and one revision; failed spatial tests or uncertain library use returns to manual coding
loop.why_not_simpler: First use native GIS model-builder and widgets. Bespoke interaction and transformation glue still require code; a fixed template cannot implement arbitrary agreed behaviour.

steps.what: Run spatial-model and mapping-interface validation tests
Review model meaning, map usability and failed test implications
Document and check the complete model package
Commit the accepted package to the internal GIS project repository

tasks.design: Test native GIS model-builder and mapping widgets in {OTHER} first. Use bounded branch-only code drafting for remaining bespoke work, run independent spatial and interface tests, and retain meaning/usability review and complete documentation before a separate version-bound repository commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spatial transformations and custom map interactions need code beyond reusable widgets.
tasks.enabler_now: Code assistance can draft bounded changes while native GIS tests validate specified geometry and behaviour.
tasks.still_hard: Correct-looking maps can conceal coordinate, topology or access-control errors.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the spatial model answers the actual question and communicates uncertainty honestly.

ambition.what: Deliver a small interactive map with reproducible spatial test examples for the requesting team.

tasks.altitude: Less implementation typing and repeated test execution; spatial design and acceptance remain human.

reach.task: Define a testable spatial model specification
reach.learn: Coordinate systems, topology and expected-result fixtures

evidence.claim: The digest describes GitHub Copilot code assistance with human oversight; it does not establish GIS-specific correctness or savings.

assumptions: Boundary is a new GIS model/mapping development package, ending at internal repository acceptance. Public deployment is a separate gated workflow. Shares are provisional, not productivity measurements.

s1 records requested_layers, source_version, coordinate_reference_system, expected_geometry, tolerance and user_action/expected_response examples from the requester and reference data. Missing expected results are established manually before implementation.

s2 specifies transformations, interfaces, access_scope and independent fixtures, with retained authoring time. s4 only executes those tests; unattended compute earns no labour saving, only currently manual invocation/comparison does.
s3 remaining time includes prompt preparation, patch reading, substantive checking and manual fallback. Source code and datasets stay in an approved processing environment.
s6 checks documentation against actual accepted code, input/output contracts and test versions after all artefacts exist. Its package hash and destination bind a1; edits invalidate approval.
research_questions: Do independent fixtures catch coordinate-order and boundary topology errors in generated changes?

already_counted.description: Draft-code and spatial-operation checking inside s3

incremental.description: Maintain independent spatial fixtures and monitor code-assistance regressions

approvals.approved_version: s6 accepted complete code/documentation/test package hash and internal repository target

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional: 25 development points minus three upkeep = 22; half benefit gives 9.5. Repository recording retains full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create analytical maps, three-dimensional renderings and geospatial plots.

steps.what: Verify spatial data, projection and vertical reference
Choose analytical method, scale and visual encoding
Set model parameters, scene layers and output layout
Run the specified analysis and generate map, scene or plot drafts
Check spatial meaning, legends, scale and apparent artefacts
Export the accepted visual into the internal project deliverables store

tasks.design: Test native processing models, scene presets and layout exports in the GIS workstation in {OTHER}. Batch only the technician's explicit rendering specification, retaining all input validation and cartographic choices; check the completed visual before separately exporting that accepted version to {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated analysis/render/export actions are often performed individually despite a stable specification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native GIS batch processing and reusable layouts can repeat specified operations without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Distortion, misleading symbol choices and uncertain source elevation need human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Spot a visually persuasive map that misrepresents spatial uncertainty or scale.

ambition.what: Provide a matched map, three-dimensional scene and plot from one accepted rendering specification.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated execution; interpretation and cartographic decisions stay human.

reach.learn: Projection, vertical datum and accessible visual encoding

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS processing and rendering can execute a defined model without choosing its analytical or cartographic meaning.

assumptions: Boundary covers visual production and internal file export; public publication is separate. Shares are provisional hands-on effort, excluding render/compute waiting time.
s1 verifies layer_id, data_version, horizontal_crs, vertical_datum, geometry_type and resolution from data-custodian metadata. Missing metadata requires manual confirmation, not guessing.
s2/s3 create method_id, parameter_values, class_breaks, symbology, camera, scale, legend_text and output_format. All parameter selection remains counted; only repetitive execution is shortened.
Test native presets before code. If current rendering and export are already batched, remove those savings. s5 checks the actual finished visual, not just successful rendering.
a1 binds accepted visual bytes, output settings and internal destination after s5; any rerender or destination change invalidates it.
research_questions: Can matched exports preserve scale, legend and datum across every output format?

already_counted.description: Check generated render against intended scale and geometry within s5

incremental.description: Maintain rendering presets and output-format checks

approvals.approved_version: s5 accepted visual version and internal export format/destination snapshot

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional: 20 rendering points minus one upkeep = 19; half benefit gives nine. Export retains full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend GIS upgrades and procedures that improve data access and usability.

steps.what: Investigate user barriers and specify representative access tasks
Measure defined retrieval and map-use tasks on candidate configurations
Judge upgrade options against usability, support and data-access constraints
Recommend procedures or software upgrades to increase data accessibility and ease of use
Submit the accepted recommendation to the internal systems review

tasks.design: Test native GIS diagnostics in {OTHER} before adding a small benchmark runner on {DATA_PLATFORM}. Measure only the technician-defined retrieval and map-use cases, retain user consultation and upgrade judgement, then submit the checked finished recommendation through a separate gate in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Options are hard to compare when the representative tasks and success measures are unspecified.
tasks.enabler_now: Repeatable timing and access checks can compare explicitly configured trial options.
tasks.still_hard: Fast retrieval does not establish usability, affordability or acceptable access rights.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the user's actual barrier and reject a technically fast but unusable solution.

ambition.what: Provide the service owner an evidence-based comparison of GIS retrieval and map-use options.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated benchmarking; recommendation rights and approval ownership remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design representative access and map-use benchmark cases
reach.learn: Task-based usability measures and access-control testing

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit retrieval and interaction benchmarks can run deterministically; selecting a suitable upgrade remains judgement.

assumptions: Boundary covers an upgrade recommendation based on existing trial options, not procurement or rollout. Shares are provisional for a case with repeated manual trials; no baseline benchmark activity is invented if the organisation does not do it.

s1 records task_id, layer, role_profile, expected_result, timeout and usability_question, including all manual case definition and user discussion. Candidate trial configurations are existing approved evaluation environments; if absent, setup must be costed before claiming a return.

s2 records task_id, configuration_version, elapsed_time, result_count and failure_code. Trial identities are authorised test accounts; no access grant or production configuration change is automated. Missing trial data are investigated manually under retained evaluation effort.
s3 retains usability interpretation and licensing evaluation. Native diagnostics precede custom code, and existing unattended benchmark runtime earns no saving.
s4 checks the final proposal, benchmark claims and target review queue after writing; any content or audience change invalidates a1. The gate only submits a recommendation, not an upgrade approval.
unknowns: Whether repeated trials currently consume technician labour
Actual user barriers and licensing constraints
research_questions: Do representative tasks predict user success rather than just map-response latency?

already_counted.description: Check benchmark implications and failure cases within s3

incremental.description: Maintain benchmark fixtures and trial-version references

approvals.approved_version: s4 accepted complete GIS upgrade proposal and internal review queue

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional: 20 analysis points minus one upkeep = 19; half benefit gives nine. Submission retains full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Program, analyse and maintain GIS applications and develop enhancements.

steps.what: Reproduce the GIS defect or define the requested enhancement
Specify the code change, analysis checks and release plan
Write the adapter, query or application patch in a branch

loop.input: Bounded maintenance specification, existing functions, schema and independent spatial fixtures
loop.output: Branch-only patch and deployment manifest with stated behaviour changes
loop.check: Technician verifies requested operation, spatial units, access handling and rollback in s3/s5; s4 runs independently specified regression tests
loop.stop: One patch and one revision; failing spatial fixtures or unclear migration effects go to manual coding
loop.why_not_simpler: Try native settings and existing adapters first. A new schema or bespoke query change still requires code with context; a fixed field mapping cannot cover every maintenance change.

steps.what: Run spatial, schema and application regression checks
Approve the final patch and deployment manifest after substantive review
Merge the accepted maintenance patch
Deploy the exact accepted patch to the internal GIS application
Write and check the completed maintenance record
Commit the checked maintenance record to the service ticket

tasks.design: Test native GIS settings and existing adapters in {OTHER} before using bounded branch-only drafting for a specific code change. Retain independent test design and substantive review, then gate merge and internal deployment separately on the final patch and manifest; the technician checks a completed maintenance record before its separate commit in {HELPDESK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Maintenance changes depend on existing spatial data conventions and application assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Context-bounded code drafting and configured regression pipelines can shorten implementation and execution.
tasks.still_hard: A syntactically correct patch can shift coordinates, break imports or expose restricted layers.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the real data semantics and recognise an unsafe migration or misleading analysis result.

ambition.what: Add regression evidence for each repaired spatial import or query defect.

tasks.altitude: Less coding repetition and manual release execution; the technician still controls the change specification and release.

reach.task: Maintain a tested spatial data adapter
reach.learn: Schema evolution, coordinate handling and rollback-safe deployment

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot offers code assistance with oversight according to the supplied digest; it does not guarantee correct GIS maintenance.
The digest reports mixed developer productivity findings; its trial percentages are not adopted as this task's savings.

assumptions: Boundary is a change to an existing internal GIS application, distinct from a new model/mapping package. Shares are provisional human effort, excluding unattended build/runtime.

s1 captures request_id, source_schema_version, sample_geometry, observed_result and expected_result from reproduction. s2 specifies affected_functions, coordinate_reference_system, field_contract, independent_fixtures, deployment_target and rollback_version. Missing expectations are resolved manually, not supplied by the coding model.
s3 retained 15 hours include prompt/context preparation, code reading, correction and fallback. s4 only executes fixtures whose authoring is fully retained in s2; no test-generation labour is hidden.

s5 reviews requested operation and rollback meaning after all code and manifest changes. Separate a1/a2 bind exact patch hash, base revision and deployment target; a merge conflict or changed manifest requires reapproval, never automatic conflict resolution.

s8 captures actual release_version, target, outcome, test_reference and residual_issue and checks the completed note before a3. Native release/ticket configuration precedes custom code; already automated actions earn no labour saving.
unknowns: Existing pipeline automation and native adapter coverage
research_questions: Does assisted maintenance reduce net labour after checking spatial meaning and rollback behaviour?

already_counted.description: Review and correct generated patch within s3
Substantive final code and manifest approval within s5

incremental.description: Maintain fixtures, assistant context boundaries and release checks

approvals.approved_version: s5 accepted immutable patch hash and repository base revision
s5 accepted patch hash plus final deployment target/rollback manifest
s8 accepted maintenance record version and service ticket identifier

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional: 25 code preparation points minus three upkeep = 22; half benefit gives 9.5. Merge, deployment and actual record save retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated GIS implementation, rendering and measurement work while retaining spatial semantics, user needs and release decisions.
reach: Help GIS analysts define spatial fixtures and developers maintain tested adapters.
role.ambitious_version: A GIS technician whose maps, model changes and upgrade advice come with reproducible evidence.
